profile_text.body:
The Algorithmic Justice League is a nonprofit founded in 2016 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. On its own site, it describes its mission as raising awareness about the impacts of AI, equipping advocates with empirical research, building the voice and choice of the most impacted communities, and galvanizing researchers, policy makers, and industry practitioners to mitigate AI harms and biases. It says AI systems are used to decide who gets hired, the quality of medical treatment people receive, and whether someone becomes a suspect in a police investigation, and that unchecked or unregulated systems can amplify racism, sexism, ableism, and other forms of discrimination.

The site points to facial recognition as a focus, noting that the TSA is expanding its use of the technology in airports and encouraging people to opt out to protect biometric rights. It also directs visitors to the Coded Bias film, which it says documents how the organization began and premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2020. The organization asks for monthly sustainers to support what it calls a movement toward equitable and accountable AI.

No products, lawsuits, or MCP servers are recorded for the organization. Its recorded location is Massachusetts.
